query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing free-text issues (Billing, Technical, Feature Request) gives a strong new grouping axis to compare resolution times across issue types, directly serving the query. All sampled categorizations are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity is a genuinely useful modeling axis for explaining resolution time and identifying where effort concentrates. Ratings are defensible inferences from described symptoms (e.g., production 502 outage=High, invoice duplicate=Low), though complexity is a judgment call the text only partially supports, so groundedness is slightly reduced.

per_column.name: resolution_efficiency_index
per_column.rationale: An efficiency index normalizing resolution time is analytically relevant to the query. However, the specific decimal values are not derivable from the row source text shown (only issue_description/ticket_id/agent_id are exposed); it presumably combines resolution_minutes with an implicit expectation, but the produced precise numbers assert a computed baseline not evidenced in the table, so values read as invented specifics.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide meaningful new axes (category, complexity, efficiency) that genuinely help analyze what drives resolution time, so usefulness is high across the board. Groundedness is strong for issue_category and reasonable for technical_complexity as warranted inference, but resolution_efficiency_index outputs precise numeric values whose derivation is not supported by the visible source text, lowering overall groundedness.
